examples.knowledge_point: Finding Unions and Intersections of Finite Families of Indexed Sets
examples.problem: Find $\,\displaystyle \bigcup_{i \in I} S_i$, given that $I = \{ -1, 0, 1 \},$ and $S_i = (i-1, \,i+1).$
examples.worked_solution:
The union of a family of indexed sets is the set containing all elements belonging to *at least one* set in the indexed family:

$$
\bigcup_{i \in I} A_i = \big\{ x\in U \: : \: x \in A_i \:\:\textrm{for at least one } A_i,\:\: i \in I \big\}
$$

where $U$ is a universal set.

Therefore, in our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{⋃}_{i\in I}{S}_{i} & ={S}_{-1}\cup {S}_{0}\cup {S}_{1} \\  & =(-2,0)\,\cup \,(-1,1)\,\cup \,(0,2) \\  & =(-2,2).\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
To write down the elements of ${S}_{4},$ we substitute $n=4$ into the expression and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{4} & ={1,2,…,4+1} \\  & ={1,2,…,5} \\  & ={1,2,3,4,5}.\end{aligned}
$$
